title: Client Retry-Hint Convergence Protocol for Metered At-Least-Once Ingest
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion combined with network retries and multi-proxy routing leads to opaque duplicate billing events. Existing server-side ledger approaches reduce duplicates but introduce reconciliation sweeps that are costly and slow. We need a lightweight, deployment-friendly protocol that reduces duplicate meter events across client retries and transient proxy failures while preserving low-latency success paths and compatibility with Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposal: Introduce a Client Retry-Hint Convergence Protocol (CRHCP). Clients include a compact retry-hint header (X-Retry-Hint) containing: a short deterministic request signature (sha256 truncated), a client epoch counter, and an HMAC signed with the client API key. Frontend proxies and the ingest gateway use a small in-memory convergence cache (TTL ~30s) keyed by signature+epoch to coalesce inflight duplicates and mark provisional reservations. Billing records are created as provisional reservations (reserve tokens) and only finalized when a single gateway instance observes commit confirmation or when the provisional TTL expires and reconciliation logic de-duplicates by signature. The protocol is opt-in per-API-key and falls back to existing ledger behavior if not present.

Why different: Instead of heavy persistent ledgers or global nonce coordination, CRHCP relies on short-lived convergence windows, client-supplied hints to increase signal fidelity, and explicit provisional->finalize flows to keep cost low and latency minimal. It also provides better cross-proxy duplicate suppression for short retry bursts and aligns rate-limiter accounting with reservation semantics to avoid over-throttling during retries.
acceptance_criteria: Clients may opt-in and send X-Retry-Hint without changing payload semantics
Frontends can coalesce >90% of duplicate retry bursts within 30s convergence window in the staging workload sampled tests
Billing exhibits no more than 1% additional false-negatives compared to baseline ledger mode and reduces duplicate charges by at least 60% for common retry scenarios
Protocol respects Dedicated and Private deployment constraints and can be disabled via config flag
Automated tests and integration tests exist for provisional reservations, finalization, and TTL expiry reconciliation
tasks: Design: formalize X-Retry-Hint header format, HMAC scheme, epoch semantics and backward compatibility
Runtime: implement convergence cache in gateway with configurable TTL and metrics
Billing: add provisional reservation record type and finalize path to metering pipeline
Rate-limiter: adapt token accounting to treat provisional reservations as soft reservations using a leased quota slot
Client SDKs: add opt-in header support and example retry policy in JS/Python
End-to-end tests: simulate multi-proxy retries, network partitions, and verify cost/latency impact
Rollout: feature flag behind per-team config, gradual ramp with instrumentation and kill-switch
notes: Trade-offs: shorter convergence window reduces memory but may miss slow duplicates; longer window raises provisional holding costs.
Security: HMAC prevents malicious replay across API keys but requires strict key rotation handling in SDKs and gateways.
Privacy: retry-hint contains only deterministic payload signature; no raw inputs are included.
Interaction with existing ledgers: provisional reservations integrate with existing reconciliation sweeps to guarantee eventual single-charge semantics.
Metricization: key metrics are provisional_reservations, finalize_success_ratio, provisional_hold_time, duplicate_suppression_rate, and billing_reconciliations

2026-02-25 - Miguel Santos: Prototype convergence cache added to gateway with kv-backed fallback. Observed 72% suppression on synthetic 100ms retry bursts in local sim.
2026-02-27 - Emma Li (Billing): Reviewed provisional reservation schema. Requested explicit finalize webhook for Dedicated deployments to integrate with customer-side commit callbacks.

2026-02-28 - Miguel Santos: Added integration tests covering TTL expiry and reconciliation path. Noted edge-case where epoch counter resets on client restart; decided to tolerate epoch reset by falling back to signature-only de-duplication for 5 minutes.
